src/specContent.js	AI scan run by CMI; R&D adds the technology view

src/specContent.js	AI use 1 — attribute language mining: AI reads category reviews (e-commerce), social conversation and search queries to extract the attribute vocabulary consumers actually use and its frequency — a cross-check on the survey hierarchy and the source of consumer-language phrasing for step 1.2.

src/specContent.js	AI use 1 — verbatim coding: AI codes the open responses (why better, why not, availability asks) against the declared attribute, consistently across every panel — the same code frame, never re-invented per study.

src/specContent.js	AI use 2 — integrity checks: attendance-log completeness, geo-tag plausibility of interviews, duplicate-respondent detection across panels, and screener-answer consistency. Flags go to the CMI field manager before the verdict is read.

src/specContent.js	AI use 2 — the red team: before the forum, AI argues the strongest case AGAINST the proposition (benchmark response scenarios, why the gap may not be perceivable). The BM answers it in writing. The forum reads both.

src/specContent.js	AI use — analog retrieval and bound-checking: AI retrieves the most comparable launches (category, price point, brand scale) from the analog base and flags every model factor sitting outside the range those analogs achieved. It flags; the BM argues; the forum decides.

src/specContent.js	AI use — assumption completeness check: AI compares the cost build against the cost structures of past propositions in the same category and flags missing lines (wastage, returns, trade load) before Finance signs. It checks completeness, never the numbers themselves.

src/specContent.js	AI use — price-event harvesting: AI scans audit data and trade news to build the register of past price events in the category (who moved, when, by how much, what happened to volume) — the raw material for the elasticity estimate and the forum's reference cases.

src/specContent.js	AI use — the threat scan: AI sweeps for early signals against this format: D2C launches in adjacent formats, patent and ingredient activity, search-trend growth of substitute formats, regulatory movement, clean-label conversation growth. Output is a threat register: each threat named, with its evidence and an assessed horizon. The register is the input to judgment, not the judgment.

src/specContent.js	Filter 1 is an argument built on consumer evidence — not a computation. The question is salience and differentiation: do consumers actually decide on this attribute, and can we visibly own it against the one strongest competitor? The data can prove the attribute matters; only reasoning can prove the advantage is winnable. So the steps below separate what CMI measures from what the Brand Manager must argue.
src/specContent.js	Filter 1 — High Success Possibility & Opportunity to Grow

src/specContent.js	Filter 2 is deterministic arithmetic on disciplined assumptions. Nothing here is a matter of opinion once the inputs are signed — the whole quality of the filter lives in who signs each input and how honestly the sensitivities are shown. The thinking is: every line of cost has an owner, every margin has a source, and the one judgment call (the quick-commerce trajectory) is written down as an assumption, never buried.

src/specContent.js	Filter 3 is the 10% volume-loss cliff rule (Part 135): smooth inflation-covering rises cost no volume; where a steep increase crosses a fixed price point (₹1, 2, 5, 10, 20, 50, 100), verified comparable volume loss cannot exceed 10%. Cliffs, not slopes. The price tested is the Filter 2 MRP — one price, one story. Fail or cannot-assess is a mark-down, never NO-GO.

src/specContent.js	Filter 4 is about direction of travel, not current size — a format can be large and dying. The thinking is detection: the evidence is trend lines and early signals, and the judgment is whether a visible signal today becomes irrelevance within ten years. This is the filter where AI adds the most, because the early signals live in unstructured data no analyst reads exhaustively.
src/specContent.js	Filter 4 — Survives Technology and Habit Shift

src/specContent.js	Filter 5 is a decomposition exercise: a revenue number is credible when it decomposes into consumer quantities that can each be checked — how many households, buying how often, at what price — and each quantity sits inside what comparable launches have actually achieved. The CMI consumer sizing model is the machine for this filter; the Brand Manager's job is to choose defensible values inside it, and the forum's job is to attack the weakest quantity, not the total.

src/specContent.js	Filter 6 is measurement science: the only filter where the evidence is generated, not retrieved. The thinking shifts from arguing to controlling — blind codes, fixed question order, declared occasions, panels that mirror the launch consumer. The enemy here is not a wrong opinion but a contaminated measurement, so every step below is a control on how the number is produced.
src/specContent.js	Filter 6 — Product & Packaging Merit Gate
